title: Foreign climate policies through export destinations

source.request:
Do foreign climate policies travel through trade?
Apakah firms yang terekspos ke export destinations dengan stronger climate/environmental policies become cleaner faster?

question: Do factories exporting to destinations with stricter environmental policy show different environmental productivity over time?
rationale: Build a dated, product-applicable policy exposure before choosing a causal claim; foreign destination sorting and demand shocks need explicit treatment.
scope: Full exact Word row, interpreted through repository minimum checks and current owner full-plan ning/full-row acceptance gates. All analysis below is planned, not executed.
unit_of_analysis: Verified establishment×destination×product×year source flows, aggregated to establishment-year policy exposure.

target_estimands.name: Primary requested target
target_estimands.formula: w_id = sum_{b=2010}^{2012} exports_idb / sum_{d,b=2010}^{2012} exports_idb; Z_it = sum_d w_id EPS_dt; q_it = alpha_i + lambda_t + beta Z_it + u_it

symbols.i: a verified establishment, never a row-number or artificial linkage
symbols.V: value added deflated with a certified appropriate price index; any single-output-deflator approximation is named
symbols.Y: gross output deflated with its certified output-price index
symbols.E: scope-defined verified physical energy in GJ; incomplete observed subtotals are separately named
symbols.C: scope-defined verified CO2 in metric tonnes; not automatically all greenhouse gases
symbols.L: workers under an annually verified employment definition
symbols.X: predetermined measured covariates declared for the particular design
symbols.g: verified treatment-entry cohort in calendar years
symbols.S: a verified trade, ownership, industry, or survival state; unknown is retained as unknown
symbols.h: product under a certified classification vintage
symbols.w_i,dh,pre: export-value share frozen before policy announcement
symbols.P_dht: certified dated policy measure and product applicability
symbols.Z_it: weighted destination EPS, on the same 0–6 scale for fully covered weights
symbols.beta: conditional outcome difference per declared exposure unit
symbols.b: one of the frozen baseline years 2010–2012
symbols.exports_idb: nominal export value under the same source currency and period within each baseline sum
symbols.w_id: fixed share of all baseline exports sent to country d
symbols.EPS_dt: OECD overall environmental policy stringency in country d and year t, from 0 to 6
symbols.q_it: the named log real-value-added productivity outcome

target_estimands.interpretation: beta is the within-establishment association between a one-point change in the weighted destination policy index and the named log productivity outcome. Baseline destination weights stay fixed; this is not a causal policy effect.
target_estimands.limits: Destination policies and economic conditions can move together. Baseline exporters are selected. The OECD index covers a subset of destinations and ends in 2020. The fully covered primary sample may differ from other exporters.
